subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance permanently use this new opt-in `turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` plus generic `onTaskTimeout` queue callback, or should it reuse the existing host compaction timeout and cooperative abort contract?
rationale: Both approaches can bound the stall, but they create different public configuration, plugin cancellation, default-upgrade, queue API, and shutdown contracts; source review cannot choose that permanent product boundary without the context-engine owner.

options.title: Sponsor the current opt-in contract
options.body: Approve the new disabled-by-default config and queue callback, then require exact-head upgrade and shutdown proof before merging.

options.title: Reuse the host timeout contract
options.body: Revise maintenance to share the existing compaction timeout and AbortSignal policy, avoiding a parallel user setting and generic callback where possible.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and close or narrow this PR if maintainers do not want another timeout/configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the current opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Approve the new disabled-by-default config and queue callback, then require exact-head upgrade and shutdown proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository lists @jalehman for Compaction and Context Engine ownership, and they introduced the ContextEngine contract and merged the closest existing timeout precedent.
